notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise prospect evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs self-hosting (current plan: run open models on EKS w/ vLLM + custom autoscaling). Key driver is predictable throughput for search/retrieval workloads and a cleaner audit trail for internal compliance.
- They were explicit: “We need a number we can put in our own SLOs—tokens/sec or an equivalent that’s defensible—plus audit logs we can hand to our governance team.”

Current stage
- Procurement/legal in progress. Negotiating throughput SLO language + remedy framework; wants clarity on what’s guaranteed vs what results in throttling.

Workload + technical requirements (from calls/notes)
- Primary: embeddings + reranking for enterprise search (batchy during indexing, spiky during business hours).
- Secondary: summarization of retrieved documents (longer contexts, some streaming).
- Traffic shape: mixed prompt sizes; they’re worried a single guarantee won’t hold if prompt lengths vary widely.
- Throughput expectation: wants predictable sustained throughput during peak (measuring in tokens/sec preferred) and a clear burst policy (what happens during a surge; acceptable throttling behavior vs “SLO breach”).
- Concurrency: multiple internal tenants; prefers per-deployment isolation and clear admission control behavior.
- Region: EU required for production. US acceptable for dev only.

Security / compliance / auditability
- Must have audit logs (who/what/when), exportable for compliance review.
- Data residency: EU-only processing for production.
- KMS integration requested (customer-managed keys in VPC).
- Retention controls: wants ability to set shorter log retention / control what is stored.

Dedicated vs Private
- Dedicated is preferred if we can meet EU residency + audit requirements without a full Private deployment.
- Private (VPC) is a fallback option if governance team requires tighter network controls.

Key decision points / questions raised
- Throughput definition: wants Redwood to define exactly how tokens/sec is computed (windowing, warmup exclusions, maintenance exclusions, customer-induced errors).
- Mixed prompt sizes: asked for guidance on how guarantees assume a context-length distribution; requested an example of how a “standard workload profile” is defined.
- Streaming: asked whether throughput SLO is measured on output tokens only, and how partial streams / client disconnects are treated.
- Audit logs: asked whether audit events include model version, deployment_id, region, request_id, and throttling decisions.

Timeline of activity
- 2025-02-12: Account created after inbound from Helio’s platform team asking about Dedicated capacity + EU region support.
- 2025-02-18: Discovery notes: procurement timeline is aggressive; they want to avoid building their own SLO dashboards for self-host.
- 2025-02-27: Procurement/legal call (Fireflies ff-2025-02-27-helio-procurement-legal). Topics: SLO definition, carve-outs, credits, and audit logs. Action item from Helio: send draft SLA clause + measurement standard references.
- 2025-03-01: Sales enablement internal sync: align on tier positioning + avoid promising bespoke guarantees outside defined tiers.
- 2025-03-04: Follow-up after internal beta announcement of Dedicated throughput tiers; Helio asked for written summary + example reporting export.

Internal guidance / positioning notes
- Emphasize that the guarantee is measurable and enforced via admission control; expected behavior under overload is throttling rather than silent degradation.
- Be crisp about assumptions: model pinned, context-length distribution, concurrency envelope, and exclusions.
- Offer a structured path: start w/ Dedicated Performance tier in EU, validate with a short benchmark/POC using their real prompt mix; move to Premium only if needed and available by region.

Risks
- EU capacity constraints could delay Premium-tier shape availability; may force either (a) Performance tier w/ clearer concurrency limits, or (b) Private deployment.
- Governance team may push for stronger auditability guarantees than what is standard in Dedicated unless we provide a concrete audit log schema + retention controls.

Open items to send Helio
- Draft throughput SLO contract language + plain-English summary.
- Tier comparison (Standard/Performance/Premium) with explicit burst policy and overload behavior.
- EU region availability notes: shapes supported + lead times.
- Audit log overview: fields, access method, retention options, and example export format.
